notes: Tested: a custom auth config created without `oauth_redirect_uri` sends `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add`. Register exactly the URI your auth config sends, or set `oauth_redirect_uri` to `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback` and register that instead.

Workspace members attempting to connect an unlisted app may see 'This app isn't listed in the Slack Marketplace...'. Resolve by having workspace admins update Settings → Apps & Workflows → App Management Settings.
If 'Require approved apps' is active in the workspace, user connection flow will pause until workspace admins grant approval.
Composio sends authorization requests to `https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize` with optional `user_scope` parameters for user-level token permissions.

assumption: An AI agent that reads conversation history, manages channels, and posts messages across customer Slack workspaces.

verdict.headline: Slack allows instant self-serve OAuth distribution, but Marketplace review is required to bypass strict conversation rate limits.
verdict.summary: Creating a Slack app takes minutes and allows immediate workspace connections via unlisted OAuth links. However, non-Marketplace apps face severe rate limits (1 req/min) on conversation history endpoints, making Slack Marketplace approval necessary for heavy production usage.

handsOnEffort.label: 2–4 hours
handsOnEffort.basis: Configuring scopes, redirect URIs, and preparing submission materials for Marketplace review.

timeToFirstConnection.label: 15–30 min
timeToFirstConnection.basis: Self-serve registration at api.slack.com/apps with immediate OAuth link generation.

timeToProduction.label: 2–10 weeks
timeToProduction.basis: Slack Marketplace review requires at least 10 active workspace installs and takes up to 10 weeks.

verdict.longestPole: Slack Marketplace submission review and meeting the minimum threshold of 10 active workspace installations.
verdict.costDetail: Slack developer tools, API access, and app distribution are free for all developer accounts.

easierPaths.condition: Using unlisted distribution without high-frequency conversation history reading
easierPaths.effect: Skip Marketplace review entirely and connect customer workspaces immediately.

factors.detail: Developers can log in to api.slack.com/apps and create an app instantly without approval or cost.
Unlisted apps distribute immediately, but Marketplace review is required for standard API rate limits on conversation history.
Slack does not require formal corporate legal entity verification to build or submit apps.
Slack performs automated and human app functionality reviews, but does not mandate third-party security audits like SOC2 or CASA.
All developer features, API endpoints, and OAuth tools are completely free to use.
No partner agreement or sales contact is needed to create apps or submit to the Marketplace.
Unlisted apps can be installed across unlimited workspaces, though individual workspace admin policies may restrict unapproved installs.
If a workspace enforces strict app management policies, non-admin users must submit an internal approval request to install.

phases.title: Register & Configure Slack OAuth App
phases.outcome: A functional Slack OAuth app with configured redirect URIs, scopes, and unlisted public distribution enabled.

steps.title: Create Slack App
steps.details: Log in to the Slack API portal at https://api.slack.com/apps and click **Create New App**. Select **From scratch**, enter an **App Name**, and choose your development **Development Slack Workspace**.
steps.agentAssist: Draft app name, description, and select optimal initial workspace.

steps.title: Configure Redirect URIs
steps.details: Navigate to **OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs**. Click **Add New Redirect URL** and enter `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add` (or `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v3/toolkits/auth/callback` if overriding). Click **Save URLs**.
steps.agentAssist: Verify exact Composio callback URLs and provide formatted redirect URI strings.

steps.title: Configure Bot and User Scopes
steps.details: In **OAuth & Permissions → Scopes**, scroll to **Bot Token Scopes** and **User Token Scopes**. Add required scopes such as `channels:read`, `chat:write`, `files:read`, `users:read`, and `channels:history` depending on agent needs.
steps.agentAssist: Provide explicit scope string list mapped to agent features.

steps.title: Enable Unlisted Public Distribution
steps.details: Navigate to **Manage Distribution → Share your app with other workspaces**. Complete all checklist items (Redirect URLs, Scopes, Information) and click **Activate Public Distribution**. This allows external Slack workspaces to install the app via OAuth without requiring Marketplace listing.
steps.agentAssist: Check checklist completion criteria for public distribution.

phases.title: Local Credentials & Initial OAuth Testing
phases.outcome: App credentials retrieved and OAuth connection validated in a developer workspace.

steps.title: Retrieve App Credentials
steps.details: Navigate to **Basic Information → App Credentials**. Copy the **Client ID** and **Client Secret**.
steps.agentAssist: Extract credentials from dashboard or environment variables for integration.

steps.title: Test Authorization Endpoint
steps.details: Construct and send an authorization request to `https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=YOUR_CLIENT_ID&redirect_uri=YOUR_REDIRECT_URI&scope=channels:read,chat:write`. Verify the consent screen loads and returns an authorization code upon user consent.
steps.agentAssist: Generate test authorization URLs and test code exchange against `https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access`.

phases.title: Prepare for Marketplace Review (Optional / High-Volume Production)
phases.outcome: Prerequisite workspace installations collected and submission metadata prepared for Marketplace listing to bypass conversation rate limits.

steps.title: Deploy to 10 Active Workspaces
steps.details: Distribute your unlisted app link to at least 10 distinct, active Slack workspaces. Slack requires a minimum threshold of 10 active workspace installs before enabling Marketplace review submission.
steps.agentAssist: Track active installation counts across workspace connections.

steps.title: Prepare Compliance & Listing Materials
steps.details: Under **Basic Information → Display Information**, upload app icons, write detailed summaries, and provide valid HTTPS URLs for your Privacy Policy and Customer Support.
steps.agentAssist: Draft compliant privacy policy summary, scope justifications, and listing text.

steps.title: Submit App to Slack Marketplace
steps.details: Navigate to **Manage Distribution → Submit to App Directory**. Fill out all required scope justifications and submit the app for formal Slack review.
steps.agentAssist: Audit submission forms and verify all required documentation URLs.

phases.title: Slack Marketplace Review Wait
phases.outcome: Slack review completed and app published to the Slack Marketplace.

steps.title: Slack Marketplace Review
steps.details: Slack performs manual security and functionality testing. Address any feedback or rejection notes sent via email or the app dashboard.
steps.agentAssist: Monitor Slack review updates and summarize feedback for necessary code changes.

phases.title: Go Live in Composio
phases.outcome: Custom OAuth credentials configured in Composio and user workspace connections active.

steps.title: Create Custom Auth Config in Composio
steps.details: In the Composio Dashboard or via API, select the `slack` toolkit, create a custom `OAUTH2` auth configuration, and input your Slack **Client ID** and **Client Secret**.
steps.agentAssist: Execute API call to register custom auth config in Composio.

steps.title: Initiate Connection and Authenticate Workspace
steps.details: Initiate a connection using the custom Auth Config ID. Complete the Slack consent prompt to link your Slack workspace to Composio.
steps.agentAssist: Generate initiation link using Composio SDK.

requirements.detail: A standard Slack account is required to access the developer dashboard.
Must configure valid callback URLs in App Settings under OAuth & Permissions.
Slack requires an app to be active on at least 10 distinct workspaces before submitting for Marketplace approval.
Public links explaining data privacy practices and user support resources required for listing.

blockers.title: Workspace Admin Restrictions on Unapproved Apps
blockers.symptom: User sees 'This app isn't listed in the Slack Marketplace...' or is forced to submit an admin approval request during install.
blockers.howToProceed: Workspace admins must disable 'Require apps from Slack Marketplace' or 'Require approved apps' under Settings → Apps & Workflows → App Management Settings, or explicitly approve the app request.

blockers.title: Strict Rate Limits (429) on Non-Marketplace Apps
blockers.symptom: HTTP 429 Too Many Requests when calling conversations.history or conversations.replies more than 1 request per minute.
blockers.howToProceed: Effective May 29, 2025, non-Marketplace apps are strictly limited to 1 req/min (max 15 objects). Submit app for Slack Marketplace review to restore normal Tier 3 rate limits (50+ req/min).

blockers.title: Missing or Mismatched OAuth Scopes
blockers.symptom: Slack API returns 'missing_scope' or 'invalid_scope' error during token exchange or API calls.
blockers.howToProceed: Ensure required bot or user scopes are explicitly added under OAuth & Permissions in the Slack developer portal and match the scopes requested during the OAuth flow.

nuances.title: 12-Hour Access Token Lifecycle when Token Rotation is Active
nuances.detail: When Token Rotation is enabled under OAuth & Permissions, Slack access tokens expire after 12 hours (43,200 seconds) and must be refreshed using single-use refresh tokens.

nuances.title: Non-Marketplace Conversation Rate Limit Enforcements
nuances.detail: Unlisted public apps operate under severe constraints on conversation history endpoints (1 request per minute, returning max 15 items), requiring architectural reliance on Slack Event API webhooks rather than active polling.

nuances.title: AI Model Training Prohibition on Customer Slack Data
nuances.detail: Slack platform guidelines explicitly prohibit third-party apps from utilizing customer Slack data to train foundation Large Language Models.

steps: Log in to the Composio Dashboard and select the `slack` toolkit.
Click **Add Custom Auth Config** and select authorization scheme `OAUTH2`.
Enter your Slack **Client ID** and **Client Secret** obtained from **Basic Information → App Credentials**.
Verify the Redirect URI is set to `https://backend.composio.dev/api/v1/auth-apps/add` in your Slack App settings under **OAuth & Permissions → Redirect URLs**.
Configure desired bot and user scopes (or use default scope configurations) and save the configuration.
Pass the custom Auth Config ID when initiating workspace connection sessions via Composio SDK or API.
